WEBSITE LAUNCH

What to include on a website before launching a new service

A new service needs more than a page with a name and a contact button. It needs a clear route from discovery to enquiry.

By Cyberfreak Software · 18 October 2026

Launching a new service is a chance to make a website more useful, not just longer. Before sharing the announcement, make sure a visitor can understand what the service is, who it helps, what happens next and how to get in touch. The same clarity makes the page easier for search engines to interpret.

Give the service its own useful page

A dedicated page gives a service a clear home. Explain the problem it solves, the kind of customer it suits, what is included and the next step. Specific language works better than a generic claim because it gives visitors the information they need to decide whether the service is relevant.

Use a page title and heading that state the service plainly. Then link to it from the main navigation, relevant existing pages and related articles. Those internal links help people find it and show how it belongs within the wider website.

Check the technical foundations before launch

  • Make sure the page can be indexed and is not blocked by a noindex tag.
  • Add it to the XML sitemap and submit the updated sitemap through Google Search Console.
  • Use a descriptive title tag and meta description.
  • Check the page on a phone as well as a desktop screen.
  • Confirm that forms, buttons and confirmation messages work.

An updated sitemap is a clear directory of the important pages on a site. It helps Google discover the new service page, although inclusion in a sitemap is not a guarantee of indexing or ranking.

Launch with a measurement plan. Record the starting point, then watch impressions, clicks and indexed pages after launch so that the next improvement is based on evidence.

Give visitors a reason to continue

A service page should connect to useful supporting content. An SEO management page could link to practical advice about sitemap care; a booking solution could show how the customer journey works. This helps visitors research before making contact, while giving the website a more coherent structure.
